quotes.text: Rockville is generally well served by a range of full-service supermarkets and specialty food stores. However residents without access to a car may face challenges, particularly those residents with lower incomes.
quotes.briefing_quote: While the 2021 Rockville Plan notes the city is generally well-served by supermarkets, it highlights that “residents without access to a car may face challenges, particularly those residents with lower incomes,” signaling an opportunity to improve food accessibility.

quotes.text: Cultivate a local food system that provides residents of all income levels access to healthy fresh food and improves food security.
quotes.briefing_quote: A primary environmental goal outlined in the plan is to “cultivate a local food system that provides residents of all income levels access to healthy fresh food and improves food security.”

quotes.text: Seek opportunities for fresh food and other goods and services for residents of David Scull Courts and other nearby residents and workers.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 plan identifies a specific need for improved access to essentials in the Southlawn and RedGate area, calling on the city to “seek opportunities for fresh food and other goods and services for residents of David Scull Courts and other nearby residents and workers.”

quotes.text: Residents have indicated concerns about potential adverse impacts of traffic, excessive on-street parking, and noise; and believe that the number and size of child care centers should be limited to preserve the residential character of the neighborhood.
quotes.briefing_quote: As part of preserving neighborhood character, community feedback in the 2021 plan highlighted a need to balance child care availability with residential quality of life, noting concerns about “potential adverse impacts of traffic, excessive on-street parking, and noise” from new facilities.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Thrive Montgomery 2050 is a blueprint for addressing historic inequities, embracing new realities, and shifting how the county should grow. The strategies aim to accommodate growth in ways that make room for new residents and improve the quality of life for people who already live here. The plan anticipates a county that will become more urban, more diverse, and more interconnected. It guides the community to leverage growth and redevelopment to create places that are more economically competitive, foster a stronger sense of trust and inclusiveness among people from different backgrounds, and improve environmental quality and public health in the process.

quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 plan highlights an opportunity to improve community well-being by designing communities that reduce challenges associated with poverty, noting, 'it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations... and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with... food insecurity, and segregation.'

quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better connect residents with local agriculture, the 2022 plan recommends strategies to 'Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.'

quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the multifaceted benefits of local food production, the 2022 plan states that 'community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas... and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Poolesville strives to preserve and emphasize our small-town charm, natural resources, and history, while continuing to promote sustainability and a strong sense of community for all. Our goal is to provide opportunities for our community members to live healthy and active lifestyles through access to essential services, parks and recreation, and high-quality education.

quotes.text: With the absence of a local grocery store to provide fresh meats and produce, the Town has encouraged and supported local farmers and vendors through farmer markets and alternative sources.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Poolesville plan highlights a key community need, noting, "With the absence of a local grocery store to provide fresh meats and produce, the Town has encouraged and supported local farmers and vendors through farmer markets and alternative sources."

quotes.text: Grocery Store
quotes.briefing_quote: When asked in a community survey what single business they would bring to town, the most common response from residents was a "Grocery Store."

quotes.text: Lack of grocery store
quotes.briefing_quote: Residents participating in the 2024 Poolesville plan's community survey cited the "lack of grocery store" as one of the most critical issues facing the town today and in the future.

quotes.text: In 2023, the Poolesville Commissioners recruited a firm to study the feasibility of developing a Grocery Co-op in Town.
quotes.briefing_quote: In response to community interest, the 2024 Poolesville plan notes a proactive step taken by town leadership: "In 2023, the Poolesville Commissioners recruited a firm to study the feasibility of developing a Grocery Co-op in Town."

quotes.text: For the agricultural sector, explore ideas such as a Food Hub, agricultural processing services, a Farm/Agricultural Incubator, and a Food Innovation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage its agricultural setting, the 2024 Poolesville plan identifies an opportunity to "explore ideas such as a Food Hub, agricultural processing services, a Farm/Agricultural Incubator, and a Food Innovation Center."

quotes.text: A Community Center that will include afterschool, senior, recreational programming, and health services for the Poolesville community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better serve local families, the 2024 Poolesville plan identifies a key community goal as creating "a Community Center that will include afterschool, senior, recreational programming, and health services for the Poolesville community."

quotes.text: A future center would provide programs such as mentoring, after-school art programs, exercise and physical fitness programs, and other health programs. In addition, there will be teen programming, such as recreational sports and games.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Poolesville plan outlines the vision for a future community center, noting it would provide programs such as "mentoring, after-school art programs... In addition, there will be teen programming, such as recreational sports and games."

quotes.text: More programs for teens – 79.74%
quotes.briefing_quote: A community survey for the 2024 Poolesville plan revealed strong support for enhancing youth services, with nearly 80% of respondents indicating they would like to see "More programs for teens."

quotes.text: Lack of recreational activities for youth
quotes.briefing_quote: In a community survey, residents highlighted the "lack of recreational activities for youth" as one of the most critical issues facing Poolesville.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Hagerstown aims to reinforce its City Center as the region's primary economic, cultural, and institutional hub. The community's vision focuses on strengthening its role as a regional tourist destination by developing key assets like a multi-use stadium, a potential hotel and conference center, and an expanded arts and events scene. Key priorities include enhancing economic competitiveness to attract new businesses, improving the quality and diversity of the housing stock to increase homeownership, and creating a more vibrant, walkable, and safe downtown to draw in residents and visitors alike.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The city envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are essential to Baltimore's future. quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2021 Maryland Food Bank survey highlighted a growing need, finding that "33% of residents said they were food insecure," an increase from 27% in 2017.

quotes.text: Today, many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners noted the lasting impact of historic policies, explaining that "many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore plan acknowledged that historic disinvestment has created barriers to food access, noting that a lack of financial investment and "limited or unreliable public transportation makes it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback revealed that in some areas, the local food landscape is dominated by "fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

quotes.text: Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing that basic needs are critical for economic mobility, the 2024 Our Baltimore plan recommended the city "Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes leading to food insecurity.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes.'

quotes.text: The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.
quotes.briefing_quote: Baltimore's food policy is designed to 'build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure.'

quotes.text: Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key initiative aims to repurpose vacant land to 'create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms.'

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. Taken together, these market reinvestments are intended to position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the vital role of public markets, the city's strategy is to 'position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.'

plan_quotes.area_name: Broening Manor, Graceland Park, Medford, and O’Donnell Heights Neighborhood Revitalization Plan
plan_quotes.community_vision: Build on the diverse culture of Broening Manor, Graceland Park, Medford, and O’Donnell Heights to create a strong coalition of unified neighborhoods seeking wellness, safety, accessibility, and enhanced economic equity for all while welcoming quality redevelopment that benefits the community with a mix of uses and amenities.

quotes.text: Access to food retailers is limited. There is no grocery store within the Neighborhood Revitalization Plan boundary.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2020 Revitalization Plan notes a critical need for improved food access, stating, "Access to food retailers is limited. There is no grocery store within the Neighborhood Revitalization Plan boundary."

quotes.text: The community gardens are planned at the northwest corner of the park, to promote access to and the availability of fresh produce to community residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address food access challenges, the 2020 Revitalization Plan proposes new amenities, noting, "The community gardens are planned...to promote access to and the availability of fresh produce to community residents."

quotes.text: A farmer’s market is suggested for the community to not only provide greater access to healthy food options, but also to create a forum for gathering and help unify the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community planners suggest that "A farmer’s market...would not only provide greater access to healthy food options, but also create a forum for gathering and help unify the community."

quotes.text: Child care can be an enormous obstacle for working parents, especially single parents. To provide affordable child care options that maintain and sustain household incomes, it is important that the community attracts additional organizations to the area to lend support.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing a significant barrier for local families, the 2020 Revitalization Plan highlights the need to address how "Child care can be an enormous obstacle for working parents, especially single parents," and recommends attracting affordable options to support household incomes.

quotes.text: Establish comprehensive family support and development programs that strive to strengthen families, promote quality child care, ensure healthy development of children through early education, and guide families toward self sufficiency and economic independence.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key implementation strategy in the 2020 plan is to "Establish comprehensive family support...programs that strive to strengthen families, promote quality child care, ensure healthy development of children through early education, and guide families toward self sufficiency."

Central to this vision is nurturing small businesses and a strong workforce, allowing entrepreneurial dreams to flourish and enrich neighborhoods with cultural authenticity.

quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2021 Maryland Food Bank survey highlighted a growing need, finding that "33% of residents said they were food insecure," an increase from 27% in 2017.

quotes.text: Today, many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners noted the lasting impact of historic policies, explaining that "many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore plan acknowledged that historic disinvestment has created barriers to food access, noting that a lack of financial investment and "limited or unreliable public transportation makes it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback revealed that in some areas, the local food landscape is dominated by "fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

quotes.text: Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing that basic needs are critical for economic mobility, the 2024 Our Baltimore plan recommended the city "Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes leading to food insecurity.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes.'

quotes.text: The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.
quotes.briefing_quote: Baltimore's food policy is designed to 'build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure.'

quotes.text: Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key initiative aims to repurpose vacant land to 'create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms.'

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. Taken together, these market reinvestments are intended to position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the vital role of public markets, the city's strategy is to 'position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Hagerstown aims to reinforce its City Center as the region's primary economic, cultural, and institutional hub. The community's vision focuses on strengthening its role as a regional tourist destination by developing key assets like a multi-use stadium, a potential hotel and conference center, and an expanded arts and events scene. Key priorities include enhancing economic competitiveness to attract new businesses, improving the quality and diversity of the housing stock to increase homeownership, and creating a more vibrant, walkable, and safe downtown to draw in residents and visitors alike.

quotes.text: In addition to the City’s 26-plot Community Garden, the City is currently exploring the reactivation and expansion of the City Farmer’s Market. The City is also now home to a Dollar General downtown, an upgraded Aldi that is walkable, and a new Lidl store that is walkable. These grocery stores have increased residents’ access to healthy food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Hagerstown's 2022 renewal application notes significant progress in food access, stating, 'In addition to the City’s 26-plot Community Garden, the City is currently exploring the reactivation and expansion of the City Farmer’s Market... These grocery stores have increased residents’ access to healthy food options.'

quotes.text: Reinvent the City Farmers Market into a seasonal program with outdoor and/or indoor venues. Support other food resource ideas being explored in the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better serve the daily needs of residents, the community's 2022 action plan outlines a key strategy to 'Reinvent the City Farmers Market into a seasonal program with outdoor and/or indoor venues. Support other food resource ideas being explored in the community.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: By embracing its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage, invaluable ecosystems and emerging opportunities, Anne Arundel County embodies the best of both the past and future, providing its residents a place where all are proud to live, work, learn, and play. The community's vision centers on strategic economic growth and redevelopment, with a focus on mixed-use, transit-oriented projects. It aims to protect the unique character of its communities and waterfronts while enhancing public access and conserving agricultural and natural lands. This vision is supported by a commitment to inclusive, equitable, and responsive government that engages all residents in building a sustainable future.

quotes.text: Much of North County is a food desert, with few locations where healthy food can be purchased.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Plan2040 highlights a significant geographic disparity in food access, noting that “Much of North County is a food desert, with few locations where healthy food can be purchased.”

quotes.text: Approximately 75,000 (13.2%) County residents live in an area categorized as a food desert, which is an urban neighborhood or rural town without ready access to fresh, healthy and affordable food.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Plan2040 background report reveals a critical need for improved food access, stating that “approximately 75,000 (13.2%) County residents live in an area categorized as a food desert, which is an urban neighborhood or rural town without ready access to fresh, healthy and affordable food.”

quotes.text: Support diverse, flexible food models that provide healthy, culturally-relevant and sustainable food in every community.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key community health goal from the 2021 plan is to "Support diverse, flexible food models that provide healthy, culturally-relevant and sustainable food in every community."

quotes.text: Improve access to healthy, culturally-relevant, sustainable and affordable food in every community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address food insecurity, the 2021 plan establishes a policy to "Improve access to healthy, culturally-relevant, sustainable and affordable food in every community."

quotes.text: Support the viability of grocery stores, local farmers markets, food banks, community food kitchens and healthy food pantries for vulnerable populations.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Plan2040 implementation strategy aims to enhance food security by working to "Support the viability of grocery stores, local farmers markets, food banks, community food kitchens and healthy food pantries for vulnerable populations."

quotes.text: Support a built environment that encourages walking, biking, and public transportation use to access healthy food, health care services, social services and employment opportunities where transportation is one of the main barriers to residents accessing health care services.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing that transportation can be a primary barrier for residents, the 2021 plan calls for efforts to "Support a built environment that encourages walking, biking, and public transportation use to access healthy food, health care services, social services and employment opportunities."

quotes.text: Work with local employers to provide job training and readiness programs as well as support services such as childcare and transportation to ensure residents can take advantage of employment opportunities in the County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 plan highlights the need to support the local workforce, noting an opportunity to "work with local employers to provide job training and readiness programs as well as support services such as childcare and transportation to ensure residents can take advantage of employment opportunities in the County."

plan_quotes.community_vision: The city envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are essential to Baltimore's future. The community aims to heal historical divides, champion vibrant and safe neighborhoods for all residents, and promote sustainable growth with a zero-waste ethos. Central to this vision is nurturing small businesses and a strong workforce, allowing entrepreneurial dreams to flourish and enrich neighborhoods with cultural authenticity.

quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2021 Maryland Food Bank survey highlighted a growing need, finding that "33% of residents said they were food insecure," an increase from 27% in 2017.

quotes.text: Today, many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners noted the lasting impact of historic policies, explaining that "many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore plan acknowledged that historic disinvestment has created barriers to food access, noting that a lack of financial investment and "limited or unreliable public transportation makes it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback revealed that in some areas, the local food landscape is dominated by "fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

quotes.text: Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing that basic needs are critical for economic mobility, the 2024 Our Baltimore plan recommended the city "Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes leading to food insecurity.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes.'

quotes.briefing_quote: Baltimore's food policy is designed to 'build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure.'

properties.tract_name: The community 1.5 miles southwest of the neighborhood of Pine Orchard

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County's vision is to be a welcoming and inclusive community renowned for its top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, abundant open space, innovative businesses, and quality opportunities accessible to all. The community cherishes its diverse environments, from historic rural landscapes to walkable suburban centers and a growing urban downtown. The collective goal is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon this unique character, grounded in sustainable development, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained infrastructure. Commitments to renew and reinvest in targeted areas will be balanced with the infrastructure needed to support communities in a timely, equitable, and fiscally-responsible way for generations to come.

quotes.text: Use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options).
quotes.briefing_quote: Focus group participants in the HoCo By Design process highlighted the need to 'use creative solutions to address food deserts' and improve access to healthy, fresh food options for all residents.

quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.
quotes.briefing_quote: During the HoCo By Design planning process, participants suggested improving food security by locating 'more food options closer to carless households,' identifying Columbia's walkable village centers as ideal locations for grocery stores and restaurants featuring locally-sourced food.

quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.
quotes.briefing_quote: A HoCo By Design participant emphasized the link between environmental health and community well-being, stating, 'Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.'

quotes.text: The Roving Radish promotes healthy eating habits in the community by selling meal kits with locally-sourced ingredients. The meal kits are available to all County residents and are offered at a discounted price to income-qualifying households.
quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan notes an innovative local program, The Roving Radish, which promotes healthy eating habits by selling meal kits with locally-sourced ingredients and offers them 'at a discounted price to income-qualifying households.'

quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a skilled and inclusive workforce, the HoCo By Design plan highlights the need to address barriers to employment, noting that entities involved in workforce development should 'partner to offer resources such as child care'.

The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes.'

quotes.text: The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.

quotes.text: Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County's vision is to be a welcoming and inclusive community renowned for its top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, abundant open space, innovative businesses, and quality opportunities accessible to all. The community cherishes its diverse environments, from historic rural landscapes to walkable suburban centers and a growing urban downtown. The collective goal is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon this unique character, grounded in sustainable development, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained infrastructure. Commitments to renew and reinvest in targeted areas will be balanced with the infrastructure needed to support communities in a timely, equitable, and fiscally-responsible way for generations to come.

quotes.text: Use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options).
quotes.briefing_quote: Focus group participants in the HoCo By Design process highlighted the need to 'use creative solutions to address food deserts' and improve access to healthy, fresh food options for all residents.

quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.
quotes.briefing_quote: During the HoCo By Design planning process, participants suggested improving food security by locating 'more food options closer to carless households,' identifying Columbia's walkable village centers as ideal locations for grocery stores and restaurants featuring locally-sourced food.

quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.
quotes.briefing_quote: A HoCo By Design participant emphasized the link between environmental health and community well-being, stating, 'Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.'

quotes.text: The Roving Radish promotes healthy eating habits in the community by selling meal kits with locally-sourced ingredients. The meal kits are available to all County residents and are offered at a discounted price to income-qualifying households.
quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan notes an innovative local program, The Roving Radish, which promotes healthy eating habits by selling meal kits with locally-sourced ingredients and offers them 'at a discounted price to income-qualifying households.'

quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a skilled and inclusive workforce, the HoCo By Design plan highlights the need to address barriers to employment, noting that entities involved in workforce development should 'partner to offer resources such as child care'.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Long Reach community is focused on the revitalization of its Village Center, guided by the Long Reach Rising initiative to create 'A Vibrant Village Center For Today.' The strategy involves systematic improvements to the center's aesthetics, attracting a variety of 'people-driven services' like businesses and non-profits, and enhancing community open spaces. The goal is to transform the Village Center into an active, desirable asset that serves as the heart of a stronger, more connected community, fostering economic vibrancy and improving the quality of life for residents.

quotes.text: Head Start, a vital early education program of the Community Action Council of Howard County, moved one of its locations to the Long Reach Village Center in 2020. The Long Reach location has approximately 5,332 square feet, allowing Head Start to increase its capacity from 38 to 80 children. Head Start provides free pre-school to eligible 3 to 5-year-old children.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Long Reach plan highlights a significant expansion of early education access, noting that a new Head Start location in the Village Center is “allowing Head Start to increase its capacity from 38 to 80 children.”

quotes.text: The application requested $245,000 for wayfinding sign system, interior, fit-outs for vacant spaces, an outdoor playground for the County’s Head Start program
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2021 Community Legacy grant application underscores the need for continued investment in early childhood amenities, proposing funding for “an outdoor playground for the County’s Head Start program” as part of the Village Center's revitalization.

quotes.text: Access to local foods has been improving but still is limited in the Village Center, with Roving Radish being the main entity. The community has expressed desire for more establishments offering healthy food options including community supported agriculture and/or a farmers' market
quotes.briefing_quote: While access to local food has improved, the 2022 Long Reach plan notes a persistent community need, stating, “the community has expressed desire for more establishments offering healthy food options including community supported agriculture and/or a farmers' market.”

quotes.text: There are not enough garden plots to meet demand, and there is a waiting list for existing plots even after the expansion of 2020
quotes.briefing_quote: Community gardening is highly valued in Long Reach, but the plan highlights a significant capacity issue, observing that “there are not enough garden plots to meet demand, and there is a waiting list for existing plots even after the expansion of 2020.”

quotes.text: According to the Columbia Gardeners, the non-profit who helps maintain the garden plots, the Maryland Food Bank harvests over 2,000 pounds of produce per year from their plots in Long Reach and is distributed to families in need.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community partners noted the community garden serves as a vital resource for food security, stating that “the Maryland Food Bank harvests over 2,000 pounds of produce per year from their plots in Long Reach and is distributed to families in need.”

quotes.text: In 2020, Howard International Grocer, a market specializing in international foods and halal meat, moved into 1,733 square feet of the Long Reach Village Center, as part of the Long Reach Rising revitalization project led by Howard County. Howard International Grocer sells fresh and frozen meat and fish, fresh vegetables, fruit, milk, eggs, snacks, and more.
quotes.briefing_quote: As part of revitalization efforts, the 2022 plan highlights new businesses that expand food access, including an international grocer that “sells fresh and frozen meat and fish, fresh vegetables, fruit, milk, eggs, snacks, and more.”

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Cherry Hill Transformation Plan documents the community's vision for its present and future. The plan seeks to guide neighborhood transformation by creating pathways out of poverty for low-income residents while building a strong, diverse community. Key principles of this transformation include ensuring no displacement of current residents, promoting holistic well-being beyond just physical changes, increasing diverse housing options, growing Black-owned businesses, and preserving the neighborhood's green, open character.

quotes.text: Lack of Grocery Store
quotes.briefing_quote: During community engagement for the 2020 Cherry Hill Transformation Plan, residents consistently identified a key weakness in the neighborhood as the "lack of a grocery store."

quotes.text: Residents have voiced the desire for a grocery store for many years. There continues to be a struggle as residents have limited access to fresh food.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2020 transformation plan acknowledges a long-standing community need, stating, "Residents have voiced the desire for a grocery store for many years. There continues to be a struggle as residents have limited access to fresh food."

quotes.text: 24 percent of MedStar Harbor Hospital CHNA respondents identified access to affordable, healthy food as a community need.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a critical gap in local amenities, respondents to a MedStar Harbor Hospital community health needs assessment identified "access to affordable, healthy food as a community need."

quotes.text: Baltimore City’s Food Policy Division of the Office of Sustainability has determined that Cherry Hill is a Food Opportunity Area, commonly known as a food desert.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data underscores the community's challenges with food security, as Baltimore City's Office of Sustainability has officially determined that Cherry Hill is a "Food Opportunity Area, commonly known as a food desert."

quotes.text: Lack of job training, workforce development, child care, and other types of support to move into higher paying/living wage jobs.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community identified a need to address barriers to economic mobility, pointing to a "lack of job training, workforce development, child care, and other types of support to move into higher paying/living wage jobs."

quotes.text: Day-to-day challenges may keep people from being engaged (such as feelings of safety, time availability, childcare).
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging barriers to civic participation, the plan notes that day-to-day challenges for residents can include securing "childcare," which may limit their availability to get involved in community planning.

quotes.text: Provide more before-and-after school care.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better support working families and student success, the 2020 Cherry Hill Transformation Plan recommends taking action to "provide more before-and-after school care."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Reimagine Middle Branch is a community-driven initiative to reconnect South Baltimore with a system of world-class parks, trails, programs, and economic development plans along the 11-mile shoreline of the Middle Branch of the Patapsco River. By holistically addressing issues of environment, health, and equity, Reimagine Middle Branch strives to realize more than Baltimore’s next great waterfront. This initiative is fundamentally about equity and justice, resilience, and health—a transformation of place supported by new connections, jobs, wealth-generation, and quality of life amenities that extend beyond the built environment.

quotes.text: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)/Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) benefits were used by 72% of households in Mount Winans, 59% in Westport, and 58% in Cherry Hill.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting the critical need for affordable food options, the 2023 Reimagine Middle Branch Plan notes that reliance on food assistance is significant in key neighborhoods, with 'Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)/Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) benefits used by 72% of households in Mount Winans, 59% in Westport, and 58% in Cherry Hill.'

quotes.text: Echoing the Transformation Plan, a combination of mixed-income housing, healthcare, and a grocery store is recommended.
quotes.briefing_quote: Building on previous planning, the 2023 Reimagine Middle Branch Plan reinforces the community's need for key amenities in the Hanover-Potee Corridor, recommending 'a combination of mixed-income housing, healthcare, and a grocery store.'

quotes.text: Start seasonal food truck program, supporting local business growth and laying groundwork for year-round Waterfront Marketplace selling culturally authentic food, products and art.
quotes.briefing_quote: To activate public spaces and create economic opportunities, the 2023 Reimagine Middle Branch Plan suggests piloting a 'seasonal food truck program, supporting local business growth and laying groundwork for a year-round Waterfront Marketplace selling culturally authentic food, products and art.'

properties.tract_name: The neighborhoods of Arrowhead, Donleigh, and MacGills Common

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County's vision is to be a welcoming and inclusive community renowned for its top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, abundant open space, innovative businesses, and quality opportunities accessible to all. The community cherishes its diverse environments, from historic rural landscapes to walkable suburban centers and a growing urban downtown. The collective goal is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon this unique character, grounded in sustainable development, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained infrastructure. Commitments to renew and reinvest in targeted areas will be balanced with the infrastructure needed to support communities in a timely, equitable, and fiscally-responsible way for generations to come.

quotes.text: Use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options).
quotes.briefing_quote: Focus group participants in the HoCo By Design process highlighted the need to 'use creative solutions to address food deserts' and improve access to healthy, fresh food options for all residents.

quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.
quotes.briefing_quote: During the HoCo By Design planning process, participants suggested improving food security by locating 'more food options closer to carless households,' identifying Columbia's walkable village centers as ideal locations for grocery stores and restaurants featuring locally-sourced food.

quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.
quotes.briefing_quote: A HoCo By Design participant emphasized the link between environmental health and community well-being, stating, 'Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.'

quotes.text: The Roving Radish promotes healthy eating habits in the community by selling meal kits with locally-sourced ingredients. The meal kits are available to all County residents and are offered at a discounted price to income-qualifying households.
quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan notes an innovative local program, The Roving Radish, which promotes healthy eating habits by selling meal kits with locally-sourced ingredients and offers them 'at a discounted price to income-qualifying households.'

quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a skilled and inclusive workforce, the HoCo By Design plan highlights the need to address barriers to employment, noting that entities involved in workforce development should 'partner to offer resources such as child care'.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Reimagine Middle Branch is a community-driven initiative to reconnect South Baltimore with a system of world-class parks, trails, programs, and economic development plans along the 11-mile shoreline of the Middle Branch of the Patapsco River. By holistically addressing issues of environment, health, and equity, Reimagine Middle Branch strives to realize more than Baltimore’s next great waterfront. This initiative is fundamentally about equity and justice, resilience, and health—a transformation of place supported by new connections, jobs, wealth-generation, and quality of life amenities that extend beyond the built environment.

quotes.text: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)/Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) benefits were used by 72% of households in Mount Winans, 59% in Westport, and 58% in Cherry Hill.

quotes.text: Echoing the Transformation Plan, a combination of mixed-income housing, healthcare, and a grocery store is recommended.

quotes.text: Start seasonal food truck program, supporting local business growth and laying groundwork for year-round Waterfront Marketplace selling culturally authentic food, products and art.
quotes.briefing_quote: To activate public spaces and create economic opportunities, the 2023 Reimagine Middle Branch Plan suggests piloting a 'seasonal food truck program, supporting local business growth and laying groundwork for a year-round Waterfront Marketplace selling culturally authentic food, products and art.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: Guided by a robust community engagement process involving thousands of residents, the vision for Harborplace is to transform Baltimore’s waterfront into a world-class destination for tourists and locals alike. The goal is to create a more inclusive and resilient place for all, re-emerging as the beloved heart of the community that showcases the very best of Baltimore's cuisine, commerce, and culture. The revitalized waterfront aims to be a safe, welcoming, and accessible space that connects diverse city neighborhoods to the water, celebrates local entrepreneurs, and serves as a model for sustainable, equitable development.

quotes.text: When we asked what would make them feel most welcome at Harborplace, they responded with answers like, 'Less violence. More security. More things for kids my age to do'
quotes.briefing_quote: Feedback from youth engagement sessions underscored the importance of creating a welcoming environment, with young people suggesting 'More things for kids my age to do' to make Harborplace a true destination for families and teens.

quotes.text: many teens and young adults also want to see local, black-owned restaurants and vendors and improved cleanliness and safety.
quotes.briefing_quote: During the 2023 planning process, Baltimore's young adults emphasized the need for an authentic culinary experience, expressing a desire to see 'local, black-owned restaurants and vendors' as part of a revitalized and safer Harborplace.

quotes.text: Retain the Authentic Character of Baltimore’s Art, Music, and Food
quotes.briefing_quote: A major theme emerging from extensive community feedback was the call to 'Retain the Authentic Character of Baltimore’s Art, Music, and Food,' ensuring the new waterfront is a genuine reflection of the city's vibrant culture.

quotes.text: Educational programming provides opportunities for young Baltimoreans to learn about healthy foods, plants, and their local ecology in a safe and engaging space.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Harborplace Masterplan envisions creating new learning opportunities, noting that educational programming should provide opportunities for young Baltimoreans to 'learn about healthy foods, plants, and their local ecology in a safe and engaging space.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: Market Center is envisioned as a vibrant, diverse, accessible, welcoming, clean, and safe part of Baltimore’s urban fabric. Stakeholders aspire for the neighborhood to become a premier international district with a mix of retail, arts, dining, and entertainment, supported by a diversity of mixed-use, mixed-income housing. The community aims to achieve development without displacement, setting an international standard for equitable, accessible improvements in a historic, inner-city neighborhood that can accommodate population and job growth and increase the city's tax base.

quotes.text: The neighborhood does not have grocery options. The only options are Potung Market, Streets Market, and a single stall in Lexington Market - all more expensive options.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Market Center plan highlights a critical gap in local amenities, stating, "The neighborhood does not have grocery options. The only options are Potung Market, Streets Market, and a single stall in Lexington Market - all more expensive options."

quotes.text: There is no full-service grocery store in Market Center, and while some Lexington Market merchants carry produce, meat, poultry, and fish, both the selection and hours are limited.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a key factor in quality of life, the plan notes, "There is no full-service grocery store in Market Center, and while some Lexington Market merchants carry produce, meat, poultry, and fish, both the selection and hours are limited."

quotes.text: For families looking to move to the area, there is also the lack of a school to account for.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better support residential growth, the plan identifies the need for family-oriented amenities, observing that "for families looking to move to the area, there is also the lack of a school to account for."

quotes.text: Food desert/lack of food resources
quotes.briefing_quote: A Quality of Life analysis identified a significant weakness in the community related to the "food desert/lack of food resources," impacting resident well-being.

quotes.text: Without a larger grocery store or a wider variety of fresh food options, many residents will be forced to rely on cars and the area will run into a shortage of storage options.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the connection between food access and neighborhood walkability, explaining that "without a larger grocery store or a wider variety of fresh food options, many residents will be forced to rely on cars."

quotes.text: Quality of Life Goal 3: Increase access to fresh food.
quotes.briefing_quote: As a core objective for improving neighborhood livability, the community established a clear goal to "increase access to fresh food."

quotes.text: Attract a grocery store to Market Center to supplement and complement existing options.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key implementation strategy outlined in the plan is to proactively "attract a grocery store to Market Center to supplement and complement existing options."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County's vision is to be a welcoming and inclusive community renowned for its top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, abundant open space, innovative businesses, and quality opportunities accessible to all. The community cherishes its diverse environments, from historic rural landscapes to walkable suburban centers and a growing urban downtown. The collective goal is to accommodate future growth in a manner that retains and improves upon this unique character, grounded in sustainable development, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained infrastructure. Commitments to renew and reinvest in targeted areas will be balanced with the infrastructure needed to support communities in a timely, equitable, and fiscally-responsible way for generations to come.

quotes.text: Use creative solutions to address food deserts (areas without healthy, fresh food options).
quotes.briefing_quote: Focus group participants in the HoCo By Design process highlighted the need to 'use creative solutions to address food deserts' and improve access to healthy, fresh food options for all residents.

quotes.text: Some participants advocated for more food options located closer to carless households. Columbia’s walkable village centers were identified as good locations for restaurants and grocery stores featuring locally-sourced food.
quotes.briefing_quote: During the HoCo By Design planning process, participants suggested improving food security by locating 'more food options closer to carless households,' identifying Columbia's walkable village centers as ideal locations for grocery stores and restaurants featuring locally-sourced food.

quotes.text: Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.
quotes.briefing_quote: A HoCo By Design participant emphasized the link between environmental health and community well-being, stating, 'Sustainability and food security mean preservation of our local farms and pollinators.'

quotes.text: The Roving Radish promotes healthy eating habits in the community by selling meal kits with locally-sourced ingredients. The meal kits are available to all County residents and are offered at a discounted price to income-qualifying households.
quotes.briefing_quote: The HoCo By Design plan notes an innovative local program, The Roving Radish, which promotes healthy eating habits by selling meal kits with locally-sourced ingredients and offers them 'at a discounted price to income-qualifying households.'

quotes.text: To ensure underserved populations can participate in training, entities involved in workforce development should partner to offer resources such as child care.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a skilled and inclusive workforce, the HoCo By Design plan highlights the need to address barriers to employment, noting that entities involved in workforce development should 'partner to offer resources such as child care'.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The North Laurel - Savage community aims to transform its key corridors, particularly US Route 1, into vibrant, walkable, mixed-use districts. Building on the vision from plans like 'HoCo By Design' and the 'Route 1 Corridor Plan', the community seeks to expand its transit-oriented development around the MARC station. The goal is to create an entertainment-focused destination that serves both existing and future residents with a mix of housing, retail, dining, and arts, while also preserving the unique historic character of areas like Savage.

quotes.text: Lack of affordable daycare centers or early childhood education providers
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 North Laurel - Savage Sustainable Community Plan identifies a need for more child care options, noting a "Lack of affordable daycare centers or early childhood education providers" as a key community challenge.

quotes.text: Investigate locating a Head Start/Early Childhood education center to support eligible children and families in the North Laurel-Savage area.
quotes.briefing_quote: As part of its action plan, the community proposes to "Investigate locating a Head Start/Early Childhood education center to support eligible children and families in the North Laurel-Savage area."

quotes.text: The 2022 LPPRP supports continuing to locate a site for a community garden in North Laurel-Savage area which would alleviate the demand on other local community gardens and locate the resource closer to community members.
quotes.briefing_quote: Referencing the county's Land, Parks, Preservation, and Recreation Plan, community planners highlight the need to "locate a site for a community garden in the North Laurel-Savage area which would alleviate the demand on other local community gardens and locate the resource closer to community members."

quotes.text: Complete design and fund implementation of a community garden in the area to address demand.
quotes.briefing_quote: To meet local needs for fresh food access, the community action plan calls for the initiative to "Complete design and fund implementation of a community garden in the area to address demand."

quotes.text: Increase capacity, awareness and coordination between local entities that address food insecurity.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support residents facing food insecurity, the 2024 plan outlines a key strategy to "Increase capacity, awareness and coordination between local entities that address food insecurity."

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Hancock aims to revitalize its economy, residential and commercial properties, and create a vibrant tourist industry by leveraging its natural assets. The community's vision is to rebrand itself as a regional tourist destination, drive economic development, and recruit and retain new businesses and industries. This will be achieved by capitalizing on the strengths of the town, including its location along the C&O Canal, Western Maryland Rail Trail, and Potomac River, to draw visitors and fuel future growth.

quotes.text: A farmers’ market occurs twice weekly at Joseph Hancock Jr. Park on Main Street and accepts vouchers; the Blue Goose Fruit Market & Bakery - just east of town limits - is a full-time proprietor of fresh, local food; there is also a full-service grocery store (Food Lion) conveniently located on Pennsylvania Avenue and Sav-A-Lot on West Main Street.
quotes.briefing_quote: Hancock's 2019 Sustainable Community Application identified a variety of fresh food sources available to residents, noting, "A farmers’ market occurs twice weekly... and accepts vouchers; the Blue Goose Fruit Market & Bakery... is a full-time proprietor of fresh, local food; there is also a full-service grocery store (Food Lion) conveniently located on Pennsylvania Avenue and Sav-A-Lot on West Main Street."

quotes.text: In addition to the two public schools, Head Start programs, a privately-operated day care and preschool, and numerous home-based childcare facilities exist.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support local families, the 2019 plan highlighted the town's existing child care infrastructure, stating, "In addition to the two public schools, Head Start programs, a privately-operated day care and preschool, and numerous home-based childcare facilities exist."

quotes.text: Food Desert
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2024 analysis of the Oliver neighborhood identified a key challenge for residents, noting that the community is a 'Food Desert'.

quotes.text: I remember a community where people knew one another; there was fresh food in the stores, there were activities that kids and seniors could get involved in at the community center, people walked around the community and kids played outside.

quotes.text: Incentivize mixed-use development along the Harford Ave. corridor to boost residential population as well as commercial retail offerings, particularly local businesses including a laundromat, neighborhood services, and/ or fresh food / grocery access.

quotes.text: The age distribution shows a significant portion of the population is either young (27% under 19) or older adults (31.4% aged 55+), suggesting a community with diverse needs in terms of education, youth services, and elder care.

quotes.text: Food access was a reoccurring theme in community surveys and engagement, finding a central location that is designed to support increased food access for the community would be desirable. quotes.briefing_quote: Stakeholder engagement for the 2024 plan revealed that "Food access was a reoccurring theme... The People's Association is looking for a location for a regular farmers market using one of the existing city-owned vacant lots."

quotes.text: Zion Baptist is a major property owner in Oliver and recently acquired a large site that formerly hosted Oliver's only grocery store which they plan to redevelop as their new sanctuary in the future.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Master Plan 2030 charts a new course for Baltimore County, focusing on redevelopment and retrofitting existing suburban environments. This approach is guided by six core principles: creating a Livable Built Environment, maintaining Harmony with Nature, fostering a Resilient Economy, practicing Responsible Regionalism, ensuring Inclusive Planning, and promoting a Healthy Community. quotes.text: The City hosts a weekly Farmers' Market every Sunday from May until October. plan_quotes.community_vision: The Greater Riverdale community aims to leverage its strategic location and the development of new transit infrastructure, such as the Purple Line stations, to foster growth and revitalization. The vision is to transform aging commercial corridors into vibrant, mixed-use centers with diverse housing options. Key goals include enhancing environmental sustainability by increasing the tree canopy and improving stormwater management, improving connectivity and safety for pedestrians and cyclists, and cultivating a distinct sense of place through branding, public art, and support for cultural heritage. The plan emphasizes creating more job opportunities, supporting local businesses, and improving the overall quality of life for all residents by increasing access to healthcare, healthy foods, and well-maintained public spaces.

quotes.text: There are fresh food grocery stores along MD 201 (Kenilworth Avenue), US 1 (Baltimore Avenue), and MD 410 (East West Highway) within a mile of the most densely populated residential areas in the existing SC Area. However, the less-densely populated areas would be outside of the one-mile boundary, making accessibility to fresh food grocery stores and healthy food options more difficult, but not unobtainable.
quotes.briefing_quote: While many residents live near grocery stores, the 2020 Greater Riverdale plan highlights an opportunity to serve all neighborhoods, noting that for some, "accessibility to fresh food grocery stores and healthy food options [is] more difficult, but not unobtainable."

quotes.text: The Town of Riverdale Park has expanded its farmer's market, which operates out of the Town Center commercial area. quotes.briefing_quote: To support food access, the community's expanded farmers market "is open throughout the year and accepts Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Electronic Benefit Transfer (SNAP/EBT), Women, Infant and Children (WIC)" and other nutrition program vouchers.

quotes.text: Initiate a community gardening program at elementary schools and unutilized vacant lot within the community. Establish a farm-to-school program to bring local foods into school cafeterias, and create school gardens.
