plan_quotes.area_name: Kentland, Palmer Park, and Columbia Park
plan_quotes.community_vision: The Kentland, Palmer Park, and Columbia Park Sustainable Communities Plan is a multi-year investment strategy designed to increase economic vitality and livability. The community's vision focuses on creating prosperity for local households and improving the health of the surrounding environment through a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects.

quotes.text: No anchor grocery store in SC Area
quotes.briefing_quote: Community planners highlighted a key economic challenge, noting, "No anchor grocery store in the Sustainable Community Area."

quotes.text: Limited access to healthy food options within SC area
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 renewal plan identified a need to address the "Limited access to healthy food options within the Sustainable Community area."

quotes.text: Capital Area Food Bank Curbside Groceries provides fresh, affordable food to the community twice a week at the Prince George’s County Sports & Learning Complex.
quotes.briefing_quote: To help meet resident needs, a local partnership ensures that the "Capital Area Food Bank Curbside Groceries provides fresh, affordable food to the community twice a week at the Prince George’s County Sports & Learning Complex."

quotes.text: Initiate a community gardening program at elementary schools and unutilized vacant lot within the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: As part of its strategy to improve resident health, the community aims to "Initiate a community gardening program at elementary schools and unutilized vacant lot within the community."

quotes.text: The Greater Washington Boys & Girls Club provides an educational afterschool program for youth in the community at the Palmer Park Community Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key community asset is the partnership where "The Greater Washington Boys & Girls Club provides an educational afterschool program for youth in the community at the Palmer Park Community Center."

quotes.text: Coordinate transportation from nearby public schools to after-school programs throughout the SC Area
quotes.briefing_quote: To support working families, the community's action plan proposes to "Coordinate transportation from nearby public schools to after-school programs throughout the Sustainable Community Area."

quotes.text: Promote and educate parents on importance of kindergarten readiness. Coordinate with local resources to connect parents and caregivers to kindergarten preparatory programs.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the importance of early education, the plan calls for efforts to "Coordinate with local resources to connect parents and caregivers to kindergarten preparatory programs."

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Greenbelt's Sustainable Community Action Plan serves as a multi-year investment strategy, outlining a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects. Local partners aim to increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, enhance prosperity for local households, and improve the health of the surrounding environment. The plan is designed to be a flexible road map for local stakeholders and State agencies to work together towards creating a more livable and sustainable community.

quotes.text: Farmers Market, Food Forest, and community gardens to provide increased access to local foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: In its 2024 Sustainable Communities plan, Greenbelt planners highlighted existing assets for nourishment, noting the community benefits from a "Farmers Market, Food Forest, and community gardens to provide increased access to local foods."

quotes.text: Daily free to low cost food service for seniors and youth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support its residents, the City of Greenbelt's 2024 plan emphasizes the importance of its "Daily free to low cost food service for seniors and youth."

quotes.text: Expand health-focused community programming, including annual vaccination and health clinics; weekly Meals on Wheels deliveries for seniors; monthly food/produce distribution; and community nursing programs for both older adults and children.
quotes.briefing_quote: Looking ahead, Greenbelt's 2024 plan identifies an opportunity to "Expand health-focused community programming, including... monthly food/produce distribution; and community nursing programs for both older adults and children."

quotes.text: Capital Area Food Bank received $32,400.
quotes.briefing_quote: Demonstrating a commitment to food security, the City of Greenbelt's 2024 plan notes it has successfully sought funding from partners, including receiving "$32,400 from the Capital Area Food Bank" to support revitalization projects.

quotes.text: Greenbelt CARES program (family assistance and support).
quotes.briefing_quote: As a key community asset, Greenbelt's 2024 plan points to the "Greenbelt CARES program" as a vital resource for family assistance and support.

quotes.text: Superior public recreation and cultural amenities and programs (i.e., parks, playgrounds, pools, gyms, classes, camps, special events, etc.).
quotes.briefing_quote: The City of Greenbelt's 2024 plan identifies a major community strength in its "Superior public recreation and cultural amenities and programs (i.e., parks, playgrounds, pools, gyms, classes, camps, special events, etc.)."

properties.tract_name: The neighborhood of Queenstown

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Brentwood envisions a future as a more livable, resilient, and equitable community, centered around the development of a new Town Center that centralizes services and enhances civic pride. The town aims to improve its environmental health through strategic stormwater management and the enhancement of green spaces. Key goals include boosting economic vitality by supporting local businesses, leveraging its Arts District designation, improving pedestrian and bicycle connectivity, ensuring quality housing options for all residents, and fostering a strong, inclusive community through diverse cultural programming and engagement.

quotes.text: Outcome: Expand health food options for residents Narrative: A farmers’ market was not launched due to market profile information and unforeseen, uncontrollable circumstances like COVID-19 pandemic. The Town provided multiple free grocery events for residents and businesses during the pandemic, including health food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: In its 2023 plan, Brentwood leaders identified an ongoing need to “Expand health food options for residents,” noting that a prior goal to launch a farmers' market was not achieved, signaling a persistent gap in fresh food access despite temporary pandemic-related aid.

quotes.text: The Town would welcome technical assistance from... Department of Health... to continue improving... access to quality food options...
quotes.briefing_quote: As part of their strategy to improve community well-being, town leaders are actively seeking partnerships and technical assistance to “continue improving access to quality food options” for all residents.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Mount Rainier envisions a flourishing and prosperous Main Street Affiliate destination city with artists, restaurants, entertainment facilities, and next-level retail establishments. The community aims to build on its historic fabric, high automobile traffic, and stable residential base by attracting new businesses, facilitating infill development in its commercial corridor, and revitalizing underutilized sites to reduce vacancies and create a more vibrant commercial environment.

quotes.text: Glut Food Cooperative established over 40 years ago and offers fresh produce and organic foods to the community: Community members earn store credit by volunteering hours at the shop keeping it accessible to community members with limited means.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 plan highlights a longstanding local institution, noting, 'Glut Food Cooperative established over 40 years ago and offers fresh produce and organic foods to the community: Community members earn store credit by volunteering hours at the shop keeping it accessible to community members with limited means.'

quotes.text: A Food Forest was also created on 31st Street by community members from the Tree Commission and Green Team along with Council members.
quotes.briefing_quote: Celebrating resident-led initiatives, the plan notes, 'A Food Forest was also created on 31st Street by community members from the Tree Commission and Green Team along with Council members.'

quotes.text: The community uses the Food Forest, local grocery Glut, and the Water Hole.
quotes.briefing_quote: When assessing local healthy food options, the plan identifies that 'the community uses the Food Forest, local grocery Glut, and the Water Hole.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: The city envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are essential to Baltimore's future. The community aims to heal historical divides, champion vibrant and safe neighborhoods for all residents, and promote sustainable growth with a zero-waste ethos. Central to this vision is nurturing small businesses and a strong workforce, allowing entrepreneurial dreams to flourish and enrich neighborhoods with cultural authenticity.

quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2021 Maryland Food Bank survey highlighted a growing need, finding that "33% of residents said they were food insecure," an increase from 27% in 2017.

quotes.text: Today, many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners noted the lasting impact of historic policies, explaining that "many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore plan acknowledged that historic disinvestment has created barriers to food access, noting that a lack of financial investment and "limited or unreliable public transportation makes it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback revealed that in some areas, the local food landscape is dominated by "fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

quotes.text: Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing that basic needs are critical for economic mobility, the 2024 Our Baltimore plan recommended the city "Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes leading to food insecurity.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes.'

quotes.text: The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.
quotes.briefing_quote: Baltimore's food policy is designed to 'build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure.'

quotes.text: Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key initiative aims to repurpose vacant land to 'create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms.'

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. Taken together, these market reinvestments are intended to position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the vital role of public markets, the city's strategy is to 'position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.'

plan_quotes.area_name: Broening Manor, Graceland Park, Medford, and O’Donnell Heights Neighborhood Revitalization Plan
plan_quotes.community_vision: Build on the diverse culture of Broening Manor, Graceland Park, Medford, and O’Donnell Heights to create a strong coalition of unified neighborhoods seeking wellness, safety, accessibility, and enhanced economic equity for all while welcoming quality redevelopment that benefits the community with a mix of uses and amenities.

quotes.text: Access to food retailers is limited. There is no grocery store within the Neighborhood Revitalization Plan boundary.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2020 Revitalization Plan notes a critical need for improved food access, stating, "Access to food retailers is limited. There is no grocery store within the Neighborhood Revitalization Plan boundary."

quotes.text: The community gardens are planned at the northwest corner of the park, to promote access to and the availability of fresh produce to community residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address food access challenges, the 2020 Revitalization Plan proposes new amenities, noting, "The community gardens are planned...to promote access to and the availability of fresh produce to community residents."

quotes.text: A farmer’s market is suggested for the community to not only provide greater access to healthy food options, but also to create a forum for gathering and help unify the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community planners suggest that "A farmer’s market...would not only provide greater access to healthy food options, but also create a forum for gathering and help unify the community."

quotes.text: Child care can be an enormous obstacle for working parents, especially single parents. To provide affordable child care options that maintain and sustain household incomes, it is important that the community attracts additional organizations to the area to lend support.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing a significant barrier for local families, the 2020 Revitalization Plan highlights the need to address how "Child care can be an enormous obstacle for working parents, especially single parents," and recommends attracting affordable options to support household incomes.

quotes.text: Establish comprehensive family support and development programs that strive to strengthen families, promote quality child care, ensure healthy development of children through early education, and guide families toward self sufficiency and economic independence.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key implementation strategy in the 2020 plan is to "Establish comprehensive family support...programs that strive to strengthen families, promote quality child care, ensure healthy development of children through early education, and guide families toward self sufficiency."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Thrive Montgomery 2050 is a blueprint for addressing historic inequities, embracing new realities, and shifting how the county should grow. The strategies aim to accommodate growth in ways that make room for new residents and improve the quality of life for people who already live here. The plan anticipates a county that will become more urban, more diverse, and more interconnected. It guides the community to leverage growth and redevelopment to create places that are more economically competitive, foster a stronger sense of trust and inclusiveness among people from different backgrounds, and improve environmental quality and public health in the process.

quotes.text: As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 plan highlights an opportunity to improve community well-being by designing communities that reduce challenges associated with poverty, noting, 'it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations... and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with... food insecurity, and segregation.'

quotes.text: Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.

quotes.text: Likewise, community gardens help to reduce the impact of food deserts in low-income areas, encourage physical activity and social interaction, and give residents who do not have yards access to nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy lifestyle.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Guided by the Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan, the community's vision is centered on three core principles: racial equity and social justice, environmental resilience, and economic competitiveness. The county strives to build racially integrated and just communities through equitable public investments and planning policies. To address climate change, the vision promotes a compact form of development with mixed uses, supported by robust infrastructure for walking, biking, and transit to make alternatives to driving more practical and attractive. This strategy also aims to enhance economic strength by creating the kinds of vibrant, well-connected places where a diverse population wants to live and work, linking all residents to economic opportunities.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Master Plan 2030 charts a new course for Baltimore County, focusing on redevelopment and retrofitting existing suburban environments. The vision is to transform underutilized commercial areas into walkable, mixed-use 'Nodes' that serve as primary centers for investment and growth. This approach is guided by six core principles: creating a Livable Built Environment, maintaining Harmony with Nature, fostering a Resilient Economy, practicing Responsible Regionalism, ensuring Inclusive Planning, and promoting a Healthy Community. The plan aims to build a future where all residents can live in a safe, healthy, and prosperous place by thoughtfully managing growth within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line and revitalizing established communities.

quotes.text: Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Essex community's vision is to revitalize its commercial corridors and waterfront areas, transforming into a vibrant live-work-play destination. The plan focuses on enhancing economic vitality by attracting new businesses, supporting the local workforce with targeted training programs, and improving the aesthetic appeal of its main streets. Key priorities include protecting natural resources, improving park amenities, diversifying housing options, and fostering a stronger sense of community through increased recreational and cultural activities for all ages.

quotes.text: Do all residents have access to healthy food options such as fresh food grocery stores, farmers markets, community gardens, etc., within the Sustainable Community? No. Essex residents have access to a variety of food resources ranging from but not limited to: Baltimore County distribution sites, BCPL food resources, BCPS resources: Student Support and Maryland Food Bank food pantry sites, WIC centers/WIC farmers markets/WIC authorized stores, Maryland Food Bank Network and pantry-to-go partners, Summer Meals sites for children, Community and faith-based food pantry sites.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Essex Sustainable Communities plan indicates that not all residents have consistent access to healthy food options, relying instead on a network of assistance programs. Planners noted that residents utilize "Baltimore County distribution sites, BCPL food resources, BCPS resources: Student Support and Maryland Food Bank food pantry sites, WIC centers/WIC farmers markets/WIC authorized stores, Maryland Food Bank Network and pantry-to-go partners, Summer Meals sites for children, and Community and faith-based food pantry sites."

quotes.text: Work with partner organizations such as the Cal Ripken, Sr. Foundation to provide enrichment opportunities for area youth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address a need for more activities for young people, the community's action plan includes a strategy to "work with partner organizations such as the Cal Ripken, Sr. Foundation to provide enrichment opportunities for area youth," ensuring children have access to positive and engaging programs.

quotes.text: Do all residents have access to healthy food options such as fresh food grocery stores, farmers markets, community gardens, etc., within the Sustainable Community? quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Essex Sustainable Communities plan indicates that not all residents have consistent access to healthy food options, relying instead on a network of assistance programs. plan_quotes.community_vision: The city envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are essential to Baltimore's future. The community aims to heal historical divides, champion vibrant and safe neighborhoods for all residents, and promote sustainable growth with a zero-waste ethos. Central to this vision is nurturing small businesses and a strong workforce, allowing entrepreneurial dreams to flourish and enrich neighborhoods with cultural authenticity.

quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2021 Maryland Food Bank survey highlighted a growing need, finding that "33% of residents said they were food insecure," an increase from 27% in 2017.

quotes.text: Today, many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners noted the lasting impact of historic policies, explaining that "many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore plan acknowledged that historic disinvestment has created barriers to food access, noting that a lack of financial investment and "limited or unreliable public transportation makes it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback revealed that in some areas, the local food landscape is dominated by "fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

quotes.text: Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing that basic needs are critical for economic mobility, the 2024 Our Baltimore plan recommended the city "Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. Taken together, these market reinvestments are intended to position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the vital role of public markets, the city's strategy is to 'position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.'

properties.tract_name: The neighborhood of Midtown-Edmonson

plan_quotes.community_vision: The city envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are essential to Baltimore's future. The community aims to heal historical divides, champion vibrant and safe neighborhoods for all residents, and promote sustainable growth with a zero-waste ethos. Central to this vision is nurturing small businesses and a strong workforce, allowing entrepreneurial dreams to flourish and enrich neighborhoods with cultural authenticity.

quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2021 Maryland Food Bank survey highlighted a growing need, finding that "33% of residents said they were food insecure," an increase from 27% in 2017.

quotes.text: Today, many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners noted the lasting impact of historic policies, explaining that "many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore plan acknowledged that historic disinvestment has created barriers to food access, noting that a lack of financial investment and "limited or unreliable public transportation makes it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback revealed that in some areas, the local food landscape is dominated by "fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

quotes.text: Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing that basic needs are critical for economic mobility, the 2024 Our Baltimore plan recommended the city "Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes leading to food insecurity.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes.'

quotes.text: The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.
quotes.briefing_quote: Baltimore's food policy is designed to 'build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure.'

quotes.text: Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key initiative aims to repurpose vacant land to 'create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: Master Plan 2030 charts a new course for Baltimore County, focusing on redevelopment and retrofitting existing suburban environments. The vision is to transform underutilized commercial areas into walkable, mixed-use 'Nodes' that serve as primary centers for investment and growth. This approach is guided by six core principles: creating a Livable Built Environment, maintaining Harmony with Nature, fostering a Resilient Economy, practicing Responsible Regionalism, ensuring Inclusive Planning, and promoting a Healthy Community. The plan aims to build a future where all residents can live in a safe, healthy, and prosperous place by thoughtfully managing growth within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line and revitalizing established communities.

quotes.text: Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Master Plan highlights the need to improve community health by resolving food access issues, aiming to 'Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.'

quotes.text: Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally.
quotes.briefing_quote: During a community engagement session, a resident highlighted a critical disconnect in the local food system, noting, 'Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally.'

quotes.text: Support an evolving agricultural industry and farming that contributes to a local food supply and conservation of agricultural land, rural open space and environmental resources in Baltimore County.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key community goal is to strengthen the local food system, calling for action to 'Support an evolving agricultural industry and farming that contributes to a local food supply and conservation of agricultural land, rural open space and environmental resources in Baltimore County.'

quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: Feedback gathered during the planning process revealed a common concern about food access, as 'Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.'

quotes.text: Implement free, full day, pre-kindergarten in as recommended by the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future for children from all households with initial focus on children from disadvantaged households.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key goal for creating a healthier community is to support early childhood development by aiming to 'Implement free, full day, pre-kindergarten... for children from all households with initial focus on children from disadvantaged households.'

quotes.text: Conduct an equity review of the community engagement meetings in order to identify factors that may contribute to inaccessibility for community members, such as meeting’s date, time, or location and the provision of translation services, childcare, transportation, or food.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges that community participation can be limited by practical barriers, and it calls for an equity review to identify factors that contribute to inaccessibility, including 'the provision of translation services, childcare, transportation, or food.'

quotes.text: Affordable Child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. Affordable Meeting space facilities (Libraries))
quotes.briefing_quote: During public input sessions, residents raised the need for a multifaceted approach to early childhood support, suggesting the county explore 'Affordable Child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. plan_quotes.community_vision: Master Plan 2030 charts a new course for Baltimore County, focusing on redevelopment and retrofitting existing suburban environments. The vision is to transform underutilized commercial areas into walkable, mixed-use 'Nodes' that serve as primary centers for investment and growth. This approach is guided by six core principles: creating a Livable Built Environment, maintaining Harmony with Nature, fostering a Resilient Economy, practicing Responsible Regionalism, ensuring Inclusive Planning, and promoting a Healthy Community. The plan aims to build a future where all residents can live in a safe, healthy, and prosperous place by thoughtfully managing growth within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line and revitalizing established communities.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The city envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are essential to Baltimore's future. The community aims to heal historical divides, champion vibrant and safe neighborhoods for all residents, and promote sustainable growth with a zero-waste ethos. Central to this vision is nurturing small businesses and a strong workforce, allowing entrepreneurial dreams to flourish and enrich neighborhoods with cultural authenticity.

quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.
quotes.briefing_quote: A 2021 Maryland Food Bank survey highlighted a growing need, finding that "33% of residents said they were food insecure," an increase from 27% in 2017.

quotes.text: Today, many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners noted the lasting impact of historic policies, explaining that "many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the ‘Black Butterfly’, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods."

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. This can be in the form of lack of financial investment to support grocery stores or limited or unreliable public transportation making it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore plan acknowledged that historic disinvestment has created barriers to food access, noting that a lack of financial investment and "limited or unreliable public transportation makes it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback revealed that in some areas, the local food landscape is dominated by "fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options."

quotes.text: Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing that basic needs are critical for economic mobility, the 2024 Our Baltimore plan recommended the city "Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes leading to food insecurity.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes.'

quotes.text: The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.
quotes.briefing_quote: Baltimore's food policy is designed to 'build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure.'

quotes.text: Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key initiative aims to repurpose vacant land to 'create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms.'

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. Taken together, these market reinvestments are intended to position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the vital role of public markets, the city's strategy is to 'position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Mary E. Rodman INSPIRE plan aims to leverage the investment in the 21st Century school renovation to revitalize the surrounding neighborhood. The community's vision is to enhance its quality of life by creating a safer, cleaner, and more beautiful environment. Residents prioritize improving green spaces, increasing beautification with more trees and landscaping, implementing traffic calming measures, and ensuring better maintenance of public areas. The plan also focuses on strengthening community unity and providing more positive programming and recreational opportunities for youth.

quotes.text: Health and Wellness: Ensure there are places for people to recreate, play, and come together; provide better access to healthy foods
quotes.briefing_quote: As part of the INSPIRE planning process, a key goal for health and wellness is to 'ensure there are places for people to recreate, play, and come together; provide better access to healthy foods'.

quotes.text: Shopping center, more grocery stores
quotes.briefing_quote: During a community mapping workshop, residents identified a clear need for improved local amenities, specifically calling for the 'shopping center, more grocery stores' to better serve the neighborhood.

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. plan_quotes.community_vision: Master Plan 2030 charts a new course for Baltimore County, focusing on redevelopment and retrofitting existing suburban environments. The vision is to transform underutilized commercial areas into walkable, mixed-use 'Nodes' that serve as primary centers for investment and growth. This approach is guided by six core principles: creating a Livable Built Environment, maintaining Harmony with Nature, fostering a Resilient Economy, practicing Responsible Regionalism, ensuring Inclusive Planning, and promoting a Healthy Community. The plan aims to build a future where all residents can live in a safe, healthy, and prosperous place by thoughtfully managing growth within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line and revitalizing established communities.

quotes.text: Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Master Plan highlights the need to improve community health by resolving food access issues, aiming to 'Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.'

quotes.text: Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally.
quotes.briefing_quote: During a community engagement session, a resident highlighted a critical disconnect in the local food system, noting, 'Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally.'

quotes.text: Support an evolving agricultural industry and farming that contributes to a local food supply and conservation of agricultural land, rural open space and environmental resources in Baltimore County.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key community goal is to strengthen the local food system, calling for action to 'Support an evolving agricultural industry and farming that contributes to a local food supply and conservation of agricultural land, rural open space and environmental resources in Baltimore County.'

quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: Feedback gathered during the planning process revealed a common concern about food access, as 'Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.'

quotes.text: Implement free, full day, pre-kindergarten in as recommended by the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future for children from all households with initial focus on children from disadvantaged households.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key goal for creating a healthier community is to support early childhood development by aiming to 'Implement free, full day, pre-kindergarten... for children from all households with initial focus on children from disadvantaged households.'

quotes.text: Conduct an equity review of the community engagement meetings in order to identify factors that may contribute to inaccessibility for community members, such as meeting’s date, time, or location and the provision of translation services, childcare, transportation, or food.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges that community participation can be limited by practical barriers, and it calls for an equity review to identify factors that contribute to inaccessibility, including 'the provision of translation services, childcare, transportation, or food.'

quotes.text: Affordable Child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. Affordable Meeting space facilities (Libraries))
quotes.briefing_quote: During public input sessions, residents raised the need for a multifaceted approach to early childhood support, suggesting the county explore 'Affordable Child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. Affordable Meeting space facilities (Libraries)).'

quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Towson Sustainable Community Action Plan serves as a multi-year investment strategy to enhance the community's economic vitality and livability. quotes.text: Additionally, the Towson Chamber of Commerce hosts annual festivals and weekly events that draw large numbers downtown. These include weekly farmers’ markets, the annual County Holiday celebration, and the Towson Fall Festival amongst many others.

quotes.text: In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.

quotes.text: Today, many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the 'Black Butterfly', are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Our Baltimore plan acknowledged that historic disinvestment has created barriers to food access, noting that a lack of financial investment and "limited or unreliable public transportation makes it difficult for those without a vehicle to travel to food retail stores."

quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.

quotes.text: Partner with organizations who can provide childcare and food security for residents who are looking for a job or training opportunity.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore's Sustainable Community strategies aim to enhance the city's economic competitiveness, foster inclusiveness, and develop its workforce by building upon existing strengths and assets. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's revitalization strategy aims to 'use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.'

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... quotes.text: The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.
quotes.briefing_quote: Baltimore's food policy is designed to 'build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure.'

quotes.text: Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key initiative aims to repurpose vacant land to 'create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms.'

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. Taken together, these market reinvestments are intended to position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the vital role of public markets, the city's strategy is to 'position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.'

The city is committed to supporting transportation efficiency, promoting access to diverse and affordable housing, and leveraging coordinated investments. A central goal is to apply an equity lens to all planning and resource allocation, targeting support to historically disinvested communities and ensuring a high standard of physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents and stakeholders.

quotes.text: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.
quotes.briefing_quote: Public health data from 2020 indicates a significant opportunity to improve community well-being, noting that 'approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.'

quotes.text: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas - areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.

quotes.text: the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transportation planners are focused on improving residents' quality of life, with proposed transit route revisions designed to 'increase access to fresh food options' for neighborhoods with lower car ownership.

quotes.text: Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges the complex nature of food access challenges, defining food insecurity as 'a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors... Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes.'

quotes.text: The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.
quotes.briefing_quote: Baltimore's food policy is designed to 'build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure.'

quotes.text: Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key initiative aims to repurpose vacant land to 'create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms.'

quotes.text: Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets in the last three years, some of which will receive reinvestment by the City, and some of which will benefit from an infusion of private capital. plan_quotes.community_vision: Market Center is envisioned as a vibrant, diverse, accessible, welcoming, clean, and safe part of Baltimore’s urban fabric. Stakeholders aspire for the neighborhood to become a premier international district with a mix of retail, arts, dining, and entertainment, supported by a diversity of mixed-use, mixed-income housing. The community aims to achieve development without displacement, setting an international standard for equitable, accessible improvements in a historic, inner-city neighborhood that can accommodate population and job growth and increase the city's tax base.

quotes.text: The neighborhood does not have grocery options. The only options are Potung Market, Streets Market, and a single stall in Lexington Market - all more expensive options.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Market Center plan highlights a critical gap in local amenities, stating, "The neighborhood does not have grocery options. The only options are Potung Market, Streets Market, and a single stall in Lexington Market - all more expensive options."

quotes.text: There is no full-service grocery store in Market Center, and while some Lexington Market merchants carry produce, meat, poultry, and fish, both the selection and hours are limited.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a key factor in quality of life, the plan notes, "There is no full-service grocery store in Market Center, and while some Lexington Market merchants carry produce, meat, poultry, and fish, both the selection and hours are limited."

quotes.text: For families looking to move to the area, there is also the lack of a school to account for.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better support residential growth, the plan identifies the need for family-oriented amenities, observing that "for families looking to move to the area, there is also the lack of a school to account for."

quotes.text: Food desert/lack of food resources
quotes.briefing_quote: A Quality of Life analysis identified a significant weakness in the community related to the "food desert/lack of food resources," impacting resident well-being.

quotes.text: Without a larger grocery store or a wider variety of fresh food options, many residents will be forced to rely on cars and the area will run into a shortage of storage options.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the connection between food access and neighborhood walkability, explaining that "without a larger grocery store or a wider variety of fresh food options, many residents will be forced to rely on cars."

quotes.text: Quality of Life Goal 3: Increase access to fresh food.
quotes.briefing_quote: As a core objective for improving neighborhood livability, the community established a clear goal to "increase access to fresh food."

quotes.text: Attract a grocery store to Market Center to supplement and complement existing options.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key implementation strategy outlined in the plan is to proactively "attract a grocery store to Market Center to supplement and complement existing options."

quotes.text: Community divestment and policy issues also contribute to a lack of food access. quotes.text: Some neighborhoods have more fast-food retailers, convenience stores, dollar stores, and drive-throughs that sell minimal or no fresh produce or other nutritious options because the zoning code does not restrict them outright, or the total number located in a particular area.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Govans Elementary School INSPIRE Plan serves as a collaborative resource for city agencies, community partners, residents, and local organizations to enhance the quality of life, health, and economic vitality of the Govans area. The plan's core goals are to strengthen housing markets, improve public safety, create networks of connection and access, foster opportunities for health and wellness, and build an environmentally sustainable neighborhood. This vision is rooted in the belief that strong schools and strong neighborhoods are mutually reinforcing, creating a cycle of community improvement and revitalization.

quotes.text: Other public and non-profit amenities for this area include the Northern Community Action Center, Govans Manor Apartments, Epiphany House Senior Apartments, GEDCO CARES Food Pantry and Career Connection.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Govans INSPIRE Plan notes that the community is supported by key non-profit amenities, including the "GEDCO CARES Food Pantry and Career Connection," which serve area residents.

quotes.text: Some accomplishments from the plan include new park infrastructure, such as the rain garden installed in 2016, the painting of the recreation center exterior in 2019, and the planting of fruit-bearing trees by the Baltimore Orchard Project.
quotes.briefing_quote: As part of ongoing park improvements, community partners have successfully implemented projects like "the planting of fruit-bearing trees by the Baltimore Orchard Project," enhancing local green spaces and access to fresh food.

quotes.text: The Govans Farmers Market has worked with small local entrepreneurs in the past and six vendors have gone on to open brick and mortar storefronts; however, none of the vendors chose the Govans area to open their business.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Govans INSPIRE Plan highlights the potential of local food-based businesses, noting that while the Govans Farmers Market successfully incubated entrepreneurs, an opportunity remains to retain them locally: "six vendors have gone on to open brick and mortar storefronts; however, none of the vendors chose the Govans area to open their business."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Master Plan 2030 charts a new course for Baltimore County, focusing on redevelopment and retrofitting existing suburban environments. The vision is to transform underutilized commercial areas into walkable, mixed-use 'Nodes' that serve as primary centers for investment and growth. This approach is guided by six core principles: creating a Livable Built Environment, maintaining Harmony with Nature, fostering a Resilient Economy, practicing Responsible Regionalism, ensuring Inclusive Planning, and promoting a Healthy Community. The plan aims to build a future where all residents can live in a safe, healthy, and prosperous place by thoughtfully managing growth within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line and revitalizing established communities.

quotes.text: Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2024 Master Plan highlights the need to improve community health by resolving food access issues, aiming to 'Reduce the number of food deserts and promote access to healthy food for all ages, particularly in low/moderate income communities.'

quotes.text: Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally.
quotes.briefing_quote: During a community engagement session, a resident highlighted a critical disconnect in the local food system, noting, 'Liberty Road is a food desert, there are so few locations to acquire fresh food and produce, with such close farmland, the County needs to find ways to get the fresh produce being grown locally sold locally.'

quotes.text: Support an evolving agricultural industry and farming that contributes to a local food supply and conservation of agricultural land, rural open space and environmental resources in Baltimore County.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key community goal is to strengthen the local food system, calling for action to 'Support an evolving agricultural industry and farming that contributes to a local food supply and conservation of agricultural land, rural open space and environmental resources in Baltimore County.'

quotes.text: Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.
quotes.briefing_quote: Feedback gathered during the planning process revealed a common concern about food access, as 'Several communities mention a dearth of grocery stores.'

quotes.text: Implement free, full day, pre-kindergarten in as recommended by the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future for children from all households with initial focus on children from disadvantaged households.
quotes.briefing_quote: A key goal for creating a healthier community is to support early childhood development by aiming to 'Implement free, full day, pre-kindergarten... for children from all households with initial focus on children from disadvantaged households.'

quotes.text: Conduct an equity review of the community engagement meetings in order to identify factors that may contribute to inaccessibility for community members, such as meeting’s date, time, or location and the provision of translation services, childcare, transportation, or food.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan acknowledges that community participation can be limited by practical barriers, and it calls for an equity review to identify factors that contribute to inaccessibility, including 'the provision of translation services, childcare, transportation, or food.'

quotes.text: Affordable Child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. Affordable Meeting space facilities (Libraries))
quotes.briefing_quote: During public input sessions, residents raised the need for a multifaceted approach to early childhood support, suggesting the county explore 'Affordable Child care vs Pre-K/ Alternatives (funding for one parent to stay home. Affordable Meeting space facilities (Libraries)).'

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Arbutus community envisions a revitalized future that leverages its strategic location near major transportation routes and its proximity to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). The plan aims to transform Arbutus into a vibrant 'college town' while preserving its small-town charm. Key goals include strengthening the local economy by attracting diverse businesses, improving the commercial district's curb appeal, enhancing pedestrian and bicycle connectivity, and attracting young families by improving housing stock and community amenities. This vision is supported by strong partnerships between local government, the Greater Arbutus Business Association (GABA), UMBC, and other community stakeholders.

quotes.text: Bring in facilities like day cares, decent shopping center, better grocery stores, good schools and parks to attract young families
quotes.briefing_quote: To help the community grow, the 2021 Arbutus Sustainable Community Action Plan identified the need to attract young families by ensuring access to essential amenities, including 'facilities like day cares, decent shopping center, better grocery stores, good schools and parks'.

quotes.text: Explore options of higher end grocery stores and cafes similar to Catonsville and Ellicott City.
quotes.briefing_quote: Looking to nearby communities as models for growth, stakeholders in Arbutus suggested an opportunity to 'Explore options of higher end grocery stores and cafes similar to Catonsville and Ellicott City'.

quotes.text: Work with partners including the UMBC, Guinness Brewery, GABA Baltimore County Arts Guild to create and support more outdoor events, health and wellness facility, dog park, farmer’s market, community center, arts and events to cater UMBC students, murals, tourists and bring more amenities to the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2021 Arbutus plan emphasizes collaboration with partners like UMBC and local businesses to enhance community life and create vibrant public spaces, including a 'farmer’s market, community center, arts and events to cater UMBC students, murals, tourists and bring more amenities to the area'.

quotes.text: Open higher end grocery stores like 818 Market in Catonsville, higher end cafes like Starbucks and quality restaurants.
quotes.briefing_quote: As a key measure of progress for community health and quality of life, the Arbutus community plan aims to 'Open higher end grocery stores like 818 Market in Catonsville, higher end cafes like Starbucks and quality restaurants' to enhance local offerings.
